new:
BCC save_on_page                \ C = 0 on the common path
    INC v_ptr + 1
    CLC                             \ (the page-crossing path: C was 1)
.save_on_page                       \ C = 0 here (TXA, TAY, EOR leave it)
    \ the data: the byte for line Y of the first cell is data[count - 1 - (line - Y)], so

summary: Move the CLC before ADC col_ptr into the rare v_ptr page-crossing path: the common path reaches save_on_page through BCC taken, so C is already 0 there.
equivalence: save_on_page has one entry besides fall-through: the BCC at 1529 (grep: no other reference; the label is local to draw_column's scope). Taken path: C=0 by the branch condition; TXA, TAY, EOR #&FF change only N and Z, so C=0 at ADC col_ptr exactly as after the old CLC. Not-taken path: C=1 (ADC #11 carried), INC v_ptr+1 leaves C, the moved CLC makes C=0 before TXA/TAY/EOR, so ADC col_ptr again sees C=0. A, X, Y, memory and every flag after ADC are identical on both paths (CLC only ever changed C, which ADC then overwrites; N/Z/V are set by ADC). BCC's offset grows from 2 to 3, far within range. Cost: 2 cycles saved on each of the 13.1 hot executions a pass (CLC measured 26.2 cycles), plus 2 cycles added on the 0.46 page-crossing executions (INC measured 2.3 cycles at 5): net 25.3 cycles a pass; same byte count. No paging, self-modified operand or data involved; the interrupt saves and restores P.
relies_on: save_on_page is reached only by fall-through from INC v_ptr+1 and by the BCC at line 1529; TXA/TAY/EOR # do not alter C (65SC12).

TXA, TAY and EOR #&FF set only N and Z, so ADC col_ptr sees C=0, just as it did after the old CLC. Not-taken path: C=1 after ADC #11. INC v_ptr+1 (&C5) changes only N and Z, then the moved CLC sets C=0, and TXA, TAY and EOR leave it there. After the ADC, A, X, Y, memory and every flag are the same on both paths: N, Z, V and C come from the ADC, and D is the same in old and new. The stack is not touched. An interrupt in between saves and restores P and the registers, and the same stores happen in the same order, so the interrupt cannot see anything different. The new BCC branches to &9C51 (offset 3) from &9C4E, on the same page, so taking it costs no extra cycle. One correction to the costing: the page-crossing path costs the same as before (INC plus CLC in both old and new). The claimed +2 cycles there is wrong, but in the safe direction. The saving is 2 cycles on each taken execution and 0 on page-crossing ones, about 26.2 cycles a pass rather than 25.3.

.last_cell
    DEC A                           \ 65C02 opcode
    STA stop_y
.part_byte
    LDA (v_ptr),Y
    STA (s_ptr),Y
    DEY
    CPY stop_y
    BNE part_byte
new:
.last_cell                          \ rows_m1 = Y - the last line: rows_m1 + 1 bytes to put back
    LDX rows_m1                     \ (X is free in columns: .more reloads it)
.part_byte
    LDA (v_ptr),Y
    STA (s_ptr),Y
    DEY
    DEX
    BPL part_byte
summary: The last cell's byte loop counts X down from rows_m1 with DEX/BPL instead of storing Y-rows_m1-1 to stop_y and comparing with CPY stop_y: 2 cycles less on entry, 1 less per byte, 2 bytes smaller.
equivalence: last_cell is reached only from cell's BCS (Y >= rows_m1, A = Y - rows_m1, rows_m1 <= Y <= 7). Old: stop_y = Y - rows_m1 - 1, the loop copies lines Y down to Y - rows_m1: rows_m1 + 1 bytes, exits with Y = Y0 - rows_m1 - 1. New: X = rows_m1 (0..7) and DEX/BPL runs rows_m1 + 1 times, the same bytes in the same order, same exit Y. On exit A, flags and X differ (X = $FF, was the record's low byte): JMP columns reloads A and flags at once; X is reloaded by TAX at .more before any use, and at columns' RTS X is dead (the part 3/2 caller PLXes it back, part 1's continues to blocks_done, which LDXes back); Y at the RTS is dead too (LDY rb_index after both JSRs). stop_y is no longer written here; its only other user, draw_column, stores it before its loop. rows_m1 is only read. Entry: DEC A + STA zp 5 -> LDX zp 3; per byte CPY zp 3 -> DEX 2. 13.13 entries + 47.53 bytes a pass (measured line cycles / per-execution) = ~73.8 cycles; 7 -> 5 bytes.
relies_on: X dead in restore_block's columns walk from last_cell to .more/RTS (PHX/PLX around the part 2/3 call, LDX back after part 1); rows_m1 <= 7 at last_cell so BPL counts it; stop_y not read after restore_block (draw_column sets it first).

X: .more's TAX reloads it; at columns' RTS the part 3/2 call is wrapped in PHX/PLX (1838-1840) and part 1's is followed by LDY rb_index / JMP blocks_done / LDX back, so restore_block still exits with X = back; Y reloaded by LDY rb_index on both returns. stop_y (&C6) no longer written here: only draw_column reads it in the renderer, after its own STA (1591 before 1603); compiled restore code never names &C6; &C6 is not in save/restore_game_zp (zplive: logic's first access after a render is never a read; frames/y/mover_x_max_high/result_high are written first in the routines read), and draw_column already leaves arbitrary values there. irq1_handler does not use &C6 or rows_m1; registers saved by the interrupt. new:
BRA columns                     \ 65C02 opcode
.compiled                           \ its entry: the kind, then the part's bottom left cell
summary: JMP columns after the last cell becomes BRA columns: 1 byte smaller, same 3 cycles while columns (&9E72) and the branch (~&9EE5) share a page; independent of the other two.
equivalence: Unconditional either way, same target, no flags or registers touched. Offset from &9EE7 to &9E72 is -117, in range (less if the other candidates shrink the code between). A 65C02 taken branch costs 3 cycles, plus 1 only if it crosses a page: both addresses are in page &9E in the current listing.
relies_on: columns and the instruction after the BRA staying in the same page (now &9E72 and &9EE7); if code before them moves so that they straddle a page, this costs 1 cycle an execution and should be dropped.

skeptics.reason: The only way in is falling through from BNE part_byte (Z=1). The JMP has no label, and no source or tool refers to its address by label+N, a table or a self-modifying store. The only way out is to columns, which reads only memory (v_ptr, rb_end) and sets A and the flags itself, so neither BRA nor JMP touches anything that is live. Neither one changes registers, flags or the stack. An interrupt sees the same state either way. Listing: the JMP is at &9EE5, so BRA ends at &9EE7, giving offset &9E72-&9EE7 = -117, which is in range. The target and the next instruction are in page &9E, so the taken BRA costs 3 cycles, the same as JMP abs. Saves 1 byte, 0 cycles, as long as columns and the instruction after the BRA stay in the same page.

Machine lens holds. BRA (&80) is a 65SC12 opcode (the file already uses BRA; DATA1 is cmos = TRUE). Listing: JMP columns at &9EE5 (4C 72 9E), columns at &9E72. New BRA at &9EE5-&9EE6, next PC &9EE7, offset &9E72-&9EE7 = -117 (&8B), in range; same page &9E, so taken BRA = 3 cycles = JMP abs 3: 0 cycles an execution, 1 byte saved. Neither touches flags or registers. No SMC targets this instruction or any label near it; nothing reads this code as data (generators read sprites, no literal addresses into &9EE8-&B39A anywhere in src). The one-byte shift of everything after (&9EE8 to the end of bank 4's code and tables, no ALIGN): no branch changes page-crossing state (scanned all branches in and into the region, including BMI compiled at &9E8E); no label or abs,X/Y table target in the region sits at a page start, so every abs-indexed read there crosses no more often than before (low bytes drop by 1 without wrapping). Caveat for the gate, not a refutation: (zp),Y walks through the straight sprites in bank 4 at run-time offsets may reshuffle page crossings by the shift (net zero in expectation, either sign per sprite), and the moved renderer variables (rb_part2, list_*, arena_top_*) are the project lens's call under 'no data moves'.

(2) The workspace moves 5 bytes. need moves &A1ED->&A1F2, so LDA need,X/Y with X/Y=14..18 newly crosses (34 slots, read in the classify and overlap loops). list_y1 moves &A2EC->&A2F1, so LDA/CMP list_y1,X/Y at 15..19 newly crosses in list_overlap's pairwise loop. ck_index,Y now crosses from 44 instead of 49. Only BEQ listed and BCS none stop crossing. Measured with passbench, seed 1, passes 500-2500, A=HEAD vs B=candidate, both built in scratch. Mean render is 24176 in both, so the 6.9 a pass never shows. Logic went 13351->13354. The worst passes got 2-7 cycles slower (1651: 120238->120240, 1653: 113598->113603, 1675: 105405->105412). Passes over 2 fields went 93->95, and fields went {1:47,2:1885,3:68}->{1:49,2:1881,3:70}: two more 3-field passes. As one change it is not faster and is slightly slower at the worst. It would need padding or an ALIGN so the compact loop, need and list_y1 keep their pages.

Project lens: not refuted. The candidate touches no PROTECTED line, no generated source and no data or table: write_column is hand-written renderer code in src/render.6502 (bank 4). The only memory it guards is its own 8 self-modified operand high bytes (src0..src7 + 2, &966D..&9697). A grep over src/ finds no other reader or writer, and nothing copies or reloads this code in place: bank 5 gets the &9300 tune unpack, not bank 4. All 8 assemble equal (ASSERT HI(hist0-8)=HI(hist0-1), hist_src_hi holds only HI(hist0-1)/HI(hist1-1)), and they are only ever written together, so src0+2 = A implies all 8 = A. Paging: the code runs from bank 4 at &96xx with ROMSEL &84 or &04. ANDY covers only &8000-&8FFF, and ACCCON's X bit affects only &3000-&7FFF, so CMP abs reads the same bank-4 byte the STAs write. Registers and flags: A is dead after it, and LDX #&C8 sets N/Z. The C that CMP sets is dead: the loop sets it with SEC/CLC before every use. V is untouched. Room: bank 4 has &B39A-&B400 = 102 bytes free; +5 leaves 97, and the ASSERTs still hold. hist0/hist1 are fixed at REN_BASE+&400/&500 and do not move. Nothing in DATA1 is ALIGNed, and outside code takes bank-4 addresses from the shared symbol table. The BEQ (&9652->&966C) and the loop's own branches stay within page &96. Behaviour is the same on every path (front end, helicopter, game over, completion, define controls): the skip happens only when the stores would rewrite identical bytes. Cycles: equal 7 against 32 (saves 25), unequal 38 (costs 6). Each push's slot is applied once to each screen, the two screens consume the same alternating slot sequence (hist_next EOR #1), and every render applies its pending entries oldest first. So about half the calls match the one before: 9.5 a call, as claimed (reasoned, not measured; the gate's passbench measures it). Possible second-order cost: the rest of bank 4 shifts by 5 bytes, which could make some other branch or table read cross a page. That is timing only, and the gate catches it. bytes_recounted is -5 in the claim's convention: the code grows by 5 bytes (CMP abs 3 + BEQ 2).

Cycles: old JSR 6 + AND 2 + TAX 2 + LDA abs,X 4 + RTS 6 = 20, new 8, so 12 saved per execution. Bytes: the call site grows from 3 to 6, i.e. -3 under the positive-is-smaller convention, which matches the claim. If the now-dead 7-byte subroutine is deleted too, the total is +4 smaller. Side effect, not a refutation: shifting the rest of bank 4's renderer by +3 changes the page crossing of a few later taken branches by 1 cycle each (BEQ taken_off &92FD, BEQ listed &97FD, BCS none &9CFD, BNE counted &9FF7). This is noise for the measured speed gate.

Not refuted. The inlined AND #&7F / TAX / LDA mover_types_width_table,X are width_of_type_A's body (render.6502:837-841), run from the same bank-4 code at the same point, so the paging state (ROMSEL, ANDY, ACCCON) is the same. The candidate's 'relies on' is wrong in one detail: the table is in game.6502 at &16D7 (main RAM), not in render.6502. That does not matter, because &16D7 is below &3000: ACCCON's X bit cannot send the read to shadow RAM, and ANDY (&8000-&8FFF) does not cover it. Results: A = width, X = type AND &7F, Y kept, N/Z from the LDA, C untouched in both versions. span_in_zone clears C, reads A and reloads X from zone_n, so nothing after the call sees a difference. The stack is two bytes shallower for the moment the call would have lasted, which nothing can observe. No protected, generated, data, zero-page or raster-timed code is touched. width_of_type_A has no other caller (grep of src and tools), but the diff leaves it in, so the region grows by 3 bytes: 6 inline against the 3-byte JSR. That matches the claim's bytes of -3 (positive = smaller). Bank 4 ends at &B39A against REN_BASE &B400 (102 free), so it fits. Everything that moves after it is referenced by label, and the page-alignment ASSERTs are on hist0 (REN_BASE + &400) and column_buffer (&0300), which are fixed. Cycles saved: JSR 6 + RTS 6 = 12 an execution. Deleting the dead subroutine as well would save 7 bytes, a net 4 smaller.

old:
.clip_test                          \ j = n - c unflipped, c - 1 flipped (c = columns left)
    LDA ds_c
    BIT dm_flip
    BMI flipped_j
    LDA ds_n
    SEC
    SBC ds_c
    BRA have_j                      \ 65C02 opcode
.flipped_j
    DEC A                           \ 65C02 opcode
.have_j
    CMP dm_jmin
    BCC to_next                     \ left of the viewport
    STA ds_j
    LDA dm_jmax
    CMP ds_j
    BCS visible                     \ not right of it
    JMP next
new:
.unflipped_j                        \ (after JMP next: reached only from clip_test)
    LDA ds_n
    SEC
    SBC ds_c
    BRA have_j                      \ 65C02 opcode
.clip_test                          \ j = n - c unflipped, c - 1 flipped (c = columns left)
    BIT dm_flip
    BPL unflipped_j
    LDA ds_c
    DEC A                           \ 65C02 opcode
.have_j
    CMP dm_jmin
    BCC to_next                     \ left of the viewport
    CMP dm_jmax
    BCC visible                     \ not right of it: j < jmax...
    BEQ visible                     \ ...or j = jmax
    JMP next
summary: Clip test: the jmax test becomes CMP dm_jmax; BCC visible; BEQ visible on j, which is already in A, so ds_j is no longer stored and reloaded. The flipped path falls through, the unflipped block moves into the dead space after .to_next's JMP next, and LDA ds_c runs only on the flipped path. Does not overlap the other candidate.
equivalence: The only entry is BMI clip_test (line 1492). .unflipped_j sits after the unconditional JMP next, so nothing falls into it. have_j keeps its name (tools/colfast.py matches draw_column.have_j). BIT dm_flip sets N from dm_flip bit 7 as before (BIT overwrote the old LDA ds_c's flags) and V from bit 6 as before. Unflipped, A = ds_n - ds_c (the same SEC;SBC); flipped, A = ds_c - 1 (the same). CMP dm_jmin; BCC to_next is unchanged. Old: visible iff dm_jmax >= j, unsigned. New: CMP dm_jmax with A=j gives C=0 iff j < jmax and Z=1 iff j = jmax, so visible iff j <= jmax, unsigned. That is identical for every value, jmax=&FF included. X (the lowest line) and Y (8) are untouched on both paths. At visible, A, C, Z and N differ (A=j, not jmax; C may be 0). visible starts with LDA b_ptr (sets A, N, Z), and C is next read only after SEC (up_cell) or CLC (raised: LDA v_ptr; CLC). At next (j > jmax), C is now 1 where it was 0. next is DEC ds_c; BEQ done; BIT, then CLC/SEC before any ADC/SBC. done is the RTS out of ren_draw_sprite. Its callers (lines 1330, 1351, 1361) do CMP #2, CLC, or RTS out of draw_mover, and draw_mover's only caller (line 1189) does LDA v_ptr; CLC before reading C. ds_j is no longer written: its only reader was the removed CMP ds_j (grep of src and tools), and the byte stays where it is. Old 35 bytes, new 31. All branch targets are within about 60 bytes.
relies_on: ds_j is read nowhere else. Carry is dead after ren_draw_sprite returns (callers at 1330/1351/1361; draw_mover's only caller at 1189). dm_flip bit 7 = flipped. Executions are from the measured window: clip_test runs 3.53 times a pass. The 1.45 unflipped runs save 2 cycles each and the 2.08 flipped runs save 1. Of the 2.75 that pass jmin, about 1.92 are visible and save 8 when j < jmax or 6 when j = jmax; the 0.83 right of the view save 6.

skeptics.reason: Checked against src/render.6502 and build/strykers.lst. Only entry is BMI clip_test (9C12); no other reference to clip_test, flipped_j, have_j or ds_j in src or tools (colfast.py only tests that draw_column.have_j appears in a profile's labels, and every clipped column still runs through have_j). unflipped_j follows JMP next, so nothing falls in. BIT dm_flip gives the same N (bit 7) and V (bit 6) as before; Z differs but is overwritten by LDA/SBC. Unflipped A = ds_n - ds_c with SEC (V from SBC, as before); flipped A = ds_c - 1 (V = dm_flip bit 6, as before). CMP dm_jmin / BCC to_next unchanged, A = j there in both. Old visible iff jmax >= j; new CMP dm_jmax with A = j, BCC|BEQ visible iff j <= jmax: identical unsigned for all values incl. jmin/jmax = &FF from draw_mover. Exits: at visible A, N, Z, C differ; visible does LDA b_ptr then TXA (N,Z), up_cell does SEC before SBC, raised does LDA v_ptr; CLC before ADC: C and A dead, V unchanged anyway. At next (j > jmax) C is 1 not 0, A = j not jmax: next does DEC ds_c; BEQ done; then BIT dm_flip and CLC/SEC before any ADC/SBC; done is RTS to ren_draw_sprite's callers: after 1330 LDX/LDA/CMP #2 (C rewritten); after 1351 LDX/LDA/BNE nothing -> RTS from draw_mover, and after 1361 -> RTS from draw_mover; draw_mover's only caller (1189) does LDX/LDY/LDA v_ptr/CLC before reading C. X and Y untouched on both paths. No stack change. ds_j (&A348) has no reader anywhere (grep) and is not read by irq1_handler; leaving it stale is harmless. Branch ranges: BMI clip_test becomes about -60, BCC to_next about -24, BRA/BPL short, all on page &9B/&9C as before. Bytes: old &9BCC-&9BEE = 35, new 8+8+15 = 31. Cycles (ds_c zp, others abs): unflipped 21 -> 19, flipped 12 -> 11; after have_j visible 21 -> 13 (j<jmax) or 15 (j=jmax), right of view 23 -> 17. With the window's counts that is 22-25 cycles a pass, about 6.1-7.2 an execution.

Recounted from build/strykers.lst (clip_test &9BCC, visible &9C14; ds_c is zero page &CC, so LDA/SBC ds_c are 3 cycles; dm_flip, ds_n, dm_jmin, dm_jmax and ds_j are absolute). Every opcode and mode is real on the 65SC12: BIT abs, BPL, BRA, DEC A, CMP abs, BCC, BEQ, JMP abs. No BBR/BBS/RMB/SMB, no decimal mode. New layout: unflipped_j &9BCC-&9BD3, clip_test &9BD4, BPL to &9BCC on the same page, have_j stays at &9BDC, BCC/BEQ visible at &9BE4/&9BE6 to the new visible &9C10 (cross a page, 4 cycles taken, as the old BCS did), JMP next, each &9BEB. BMI clip_test (&9C0E to &9BD4) still crosses a page: 4 cycles, as before. Up to have_j: unflipped 21 old vs 19 new (-2), flipped 12 vs 11 (-1). From have_j: visible with j<jmax 22 vs 14 (-8), j=jmax 22 vs 16 (-6), right of view 23 vs 17 (-6), left of view unchanged. Bytes 35 -> 31 (-4). Semantics checked: visible iff j <= jmax unsigned in both. X and Y untouched. A, N and Z are overwritten at visible (LDA b_ptr) and at next. V comes from BIT dm_flip on both. C is dead after visible (SEC at up_cell, CLC before the ADC after raised). On the next->done->RTS path C is now 1 where it was 0, but each ren_draw_sprite caller (1330, 1351, 1361) overwrites it or returns through draw_mover, whose only caller (1189) does CLC first. ds_j has no other reader in src or tools, and nothing writes into the moved code except symbolic operands (mask_operand/pix_operand), which still assemble correctly. Not counted in the claim: everything after it in bank 4 moves down 4 bytes. That puts LDA straight_sprite_hi,X (base &A501 -> &A4FD) across a page for sprite >= 3, about +4.5 cycles a pass (the window shows 18.2 cycles there). compact's BNE len_low (&A000 -> &9FFC, target &A001) now crosses when taken, about +3.7 a pass. sfx50's ramp read may gain about +1. list_y1 (&A2EC -> &A2E8) loses a few crossings. So the net is about +15 cycles a pass, not 24. It is still a saving, and the serial gate's passbench will measure the true figure.

Checked against src/render.6502 1441-1640 and the callers. The only way into clip_test is BMI clip_test at on_same_page; .unflipped_j follows to_next's unconditional JMP next, so nothing falls into it, and flipped_j had no other referrer. j is the same on both paths (ds_n - ds_c with SEC; ds_c - 1). visible iff jmax >= j unsigned in both (CMP dm_jmax; BCC/BEQ = j <= jmax). X (lowest line) and Y (8) untouched; V from BIT dm_flip as before (CMP leaves V). At visible A/C/Z/N are overwritten (LDA b_ptr; SEC in up_cell; CLC before ADC at raised) and C already varied on the no-clip entry. At next C is overwritten before use (CLC/SEC); at done C reaches the callers, which read it only after CMP #2 (first part), not at all (second, BNE/RTS), or after CLC (draw_mover's caller at 1189); C at done already varied in the old code. ds_j is written nowhere else and read nowhere else (src, tools); its byte stays. Not PROTECTED, not generated, not data, not raster-timed; bank 4 renderer code, no ROMSEL/ACCCON change and the only memory access removed is the dead STA ds_j. Shrinks by 4 bytes (&9BCC-&9BEE was 35), so Room is fine. Labels colfast.py and the profilers use (have_j, each, visible, byte) all survive. Cycle recount from the listing (&9BCC..): unflipped saves 3 not 2 (old LDA4 BIT4 BMI2 LDA4 SEC2 SBC4 BRA3 = 23; new BIT4 BPL3 + 13 = 20), flipped saves 1; BCS visible (old) and BCC/BEQ visible (new) both cross &9C00, so the visible savings stay 8 (j<jmax) and 6 (j=jmax), right-of-view 6. About 25.8 cycles a pass, 7.3 a clip_test.

old:
BCC to_next
    INC col_ptr + 1
.to_next
    JMP next
new:
BCS empty_hi                    \ the page crossed (rare)
.to_next
    JMP next
.empty_hi
    INC col_ptr + 1
    BRA to_next                     \ 65C02 opcode
summary: Empty column: the common path, where no page is crossed, falls through BCS (2 cycles) into JMP next instead of taking BCC (3 cycles) to it. The page-cross INC moves out of line. Saves 1 cycle an empty column; 2 bytes larger. Does not overlap candidate 1: both apply, and candidate 1's .unflipped_j then follows BRA to_next.
equivalence: Reached only by falling from STA col_ptr after LDA col_ptr; CLC; ADC #2 (the empty path). .to_next stays the target of BCC to_next in have_j, with the same meaning (JMP next). No carry: falls to JMP next exactly as the taken BCC did. Carry: INC col_ptr+1, then BRA to_next -> JMP next, as before. A, X, Y and C are identical on reaching next: C=1 on the carry path in both versions, 0 otherwise, and INC/BRA/JMP leave C alone. Z/N differ only on the carry path, and next starts with DEC ds_c. empty_hi is a new label, unique in the draw_column scope.
relies_on: Measured: STA col_ptr runs 4.17 times a pass and BCC is always taken (the profile never executes the INC), so the rare path's +4 cycles do not count. Bank 4 has 2 bytes to spare under the render ASSERT (below &B600).

skeptics.reason: Semantics hold on every path. Entries: .empty only from BEQ empty in .each (line 1474); line 1443 is BRA each so nothing falls into .empty; .to_next is referenced only by BCC to_next in have_j (line 1465) and the new BRA (no other users in src/, no tables, no label+N). Exit is always JMP next, no stack use. No-carry path: old BCC taken -> JMP next, new BCS not taken -> JMP next: A, X, Y, memory, C=0, V and N/Z (from ADC) identical. Carry path: same single INC col_ptr+1 write; N/Z from the INC in both (BRA/JMP touch no flags), C=1 and V from ADC in both, so every flag is identical. Nothing an interrupt could see differs: same stores in the same order. Self-modified operands move +2 but are written only by label. Built the candidate in a scratch copy (RELEASE=1, -Shift 256 -ShiftEnd with/without DEBUG_FULLREDRAW, DEBUG_LIVES+FULLREDRAW): all assemble. Recount from the listing: BCS &9BC5 not taken 2 + JMP 3 = 5 vs BCC taken same page 3 + JMP 3 = 6: 1 saved; carry path 14 vs 10 (+4). Bytes +2 (saved -2). Caveat for the gate, not a refutation: the 2 bytes shift everything after draw_column.empty in bank 4 by +2 (render workspace, sprite_column_count, ck_* tables, straight_sprite_lo/hi, straight sprite data). Behaviour is unchanged (all by label), but page crossings change: BCS none at &9CFF no longer crosses when taken (-1), LDA straight_sprite_lo,X now crosses for X=&49,&4A (+1), LDX ck_index,Y for Y=&2F,&30 (+1), and (col_ptr)/(d_ptr),Y crossings in sprite data shift. So the net per pass is not exactly 4.17; the gate's pcprof must decide, and the project skeptic should weigh 'no data moves' against growth within render's free space.

Machine lens holds. All opcodes real on the 65SC12 (BCS, INC zp, BRA = 65C02 in a cmos = TRUE section; no Rockwell bit ops). Recount at the current listing (.empty &9BBE): old BCC to_next at &9BC5 is taken to &9BC9 on the same page = 3 cycles, new BCS empty_hi not taken = 2, so 1 cycle saved an execution with no page-crossing case on either side; the carry path goes from 2+5 = 7 to 3+5+3 = 11 (+4). Bytes: old 4 (BCC+INC), new 6 (BCS+INC+BRA), +2 (bytes saved -2). Branch ranges fine: the candidate assembles (BCS +3, BRA back, have_j's BCC to_next now &E4 back), and bank 4 stays under its ASSERTs. .empty is reached only by BEQ empty from .each; to_next keeps its meaning (JMP next) for have_j. No self-modified operand moves meaning: mask_operand/pix_operand(_2), header_hi etc. are written by label, so the +2 shift is followed. Not counted by the claim: the +2 bytes move everything after it in bank 4 (need, list_y1, ck_index, straight_sprite_lo sit near page ends; the straight sprite data; BCS none at compiled_part stops crossing a page), so the real change differs from 4.17 a pass. Measured (pcprof --detail, a09d79a + this candidate vs ctl-2521688 bench, 2026-10-17): seed 1 43036.1 -> 43034.16 (1.94 a pass saved), RIGHT 49856.57 -> 49839.5 (17.07 saved). Faster on both games, so not refuted, but the claim's 4.17 is not the measured figure.

old:
.up_cell
    TAX
    LDA s_ptr
    SEC
    SBC #&80
    STA s_ptr
    LDA s_ptr + 1
    SBC #&02
    CMP #&40
    BCS up_in_ring
    ADC #&40
.up_in_ring
    STA s_ptr + 1
    TXA
    CLC
    ADC #8
    BCC up_cell
.raised                             \ A = the line of the lowest byte drawn
    TAX
    ORA s_ptr                       \ the record's address
new:
.up_cell                            \ X = the line, negative: a cell up for each 8
    LDA s_ptr
    SEC
    SBC #&80
    STA s_ptr
    LDA s_ptr + 1
    SBC #&02                        \ C stays 1: the high byte is &40 or more
    ORA #&40                        \ round the 16K: &3D-&3F to &7D-&7F, &40-&7F unchanged
    STA s_ptr + 1
    TXA
    ADC #7                          \ C = 1: + 8
    TAX
    BCC up_cell
.raised                             \ A = X = the line of the lowest byte drawn
    ORA s_ptr                       \ the record's address
summary: Drop the TAX at .raised (A = X already on the hot BPL path; the cell-up loop does its TAX at the bottom instead of the top), and in that loop replace CMP/BCS/ADC #&40 with ORA #&40 and use the known C = 1 after SBC #&02 for ADC #7 in place of CLC; ADC #8. Overlaps the second candidate (its alternative).
equivalence: Hot path (TXA; BPL raised, ~11.3 a pass): A = X already from the TXA, so the TAX at .raised is redundant. Loop path: the TAX at the top of up_cell moves to after the ADC, so each iteration still updates X (on entry X = the line: from the TAX at 1482, or via clip_test -> BCS visible, which never touches X), and on the fall-through out of the loop A = X, as the removed TAX at .raised gave. TAX does not touch C, so BCC tests the ADC's carry as before. In the loop, SBC #&02 on a high byte of &40-&7F (minus at most 3 with the low byte's borrow) never borrows, so C = 1 after it; ORA leaves C alone, so TXA; ADC #7 gives the same A and carry as TXA; CLC; ADC #8. ORA #&40 equals CMP #&40/BCS/ADC #&40 (C=0 on that path) for every A in &00-&7F (A < &40: bit 6 clear, so A + &40 = A OR &40; &40-&7F: unchanged by both). After .raised: A = X = the line and Y = 8 as before; C is not live (next C use is the CLC at 1526); N/Z come from the ORA as before; s_ptr/s_ptr+1 hold the same values. No other references to up_cell, up_in_ring or raised anywhere in src/ (up_in_ring is removed). Same RAM, same paging, no new RAM.
relies_on: s_ptr+1 (copied from b_ptr+1) is in the screen ring &40-&7F on entry to up_cell, as everywhere in the renderer (raise_address, the flipped adjust, step_back/forward and compiled_part's unsafe restore all keep b_ptr+1 in &40-&7F; movers' screen addresses are in &40-&7F). Cycles: 2 on each of the 13.1 executions of .raised a pass (26.2) plus 5 an iteration of the loop (CLC 2; CMP+BCS taken 5 -> ORA 2) on ~1.9 iterations a pass (9.5).

skeptics.reason: Entries: only fall-through from TXA/BPL raised at 1498 (A = X = the line; X from the TAX at 1482, untouched on the clip_test -> BCS visible path) and the loop's own BCC; no other references to up_cell/up_in_ring/raised in src or tools; no self-modification or tables point into the range. Loop: X now updated by TAX after ADC instead of at the top, so X = A at every BCC and at the fall-through into .raised, as the removed TAX there gave. C after SBC #&02 is 1 whenever s_ptr+1 >= 3; ORA keeps C, so ADC #7 with C=1 gives the same 9-bit sum, so the same A, C, N, Z and V as CLC; ADC #8. ORA #&40 equals CMP #&40/BCS/ADC #&40 for every result in &00-&7F and &C0-&FF; they differ only if s_ptr+1 is in &00-&02 or &82-&C2 on entry, which cannot happen: s_ptr+1 = b_ptr+1, from raise_address (which keeps dm_scr_hi, a mover screen address, in &40-&7F and wraps it), the flipped adjust, step_back/forward (wrap to &7F/&40) and compiled_part's unsafe restore of the same b_ptr; the loop itself keeps it in &40-&7F, and old code at such a value would already write outside the screen. After .raised: A = X = the line, ORA gives the same N/Z, C dead until the CLC at 1526, V identical anyway; s_ptr/s_ptr+1 receive the same values in the same order, so an interrupt sees nothing different; no stack use. Cycles: 2 a .raised execution; loop iteration old 9 (10 wrapping) vs new 4, so 5 (6) more an iteration. Bytes: 9 old vs 3 new: 6.

Not refuted. Every opcode is plain NMOS/65SC12 (LDA/STA zp, SEC, SBC/ORA/ADC #imm, TXA/TAX, BCC, BPL); no page crossings in the changed lines (zp and immediate only). Listing: BPL raised at &9C1D, up_cell &9C1F; new raised = &9C34 and BCC at &9C32 -> &9C1F, all page &9C, so no branch takes a page-cross cycle; ranges tiny. Bytes: old up_cell..TAX at raised = 27 (&9C1F-&9C39), new 21: 6 saved. Cycles: hot path (TXA; BPL raised taken) loses the TAX at raised: 2. Loop iteration: old 31 (no wrap) / 32 (wrap) + BCC, new 26 + BCC: 5 / 6 a pass round the loop, the TAX moved not removed, the exit's TAX gone (counted in the 2). Semantics on the machine: C = 1 after SBC #&02 needs s_ptr+1 >= 3 on each iteration; b_ptr+1 comes from raise_address (in-cell path passes movers_screen_address_high through; the game builds those with its wrapping add/subtract helpers and the original plots there, so &40-&7F), the flipped adjust (BPL/-&40), step_forward (BPL else &40), step_back (<&40 -> &7F) and compiled_part's unsafe restore, all &40-&7F; ORA #&40 then keeps s_ptr+1 in &40-&7F, so inductively C = 1 and ORA #&40 = the old CMP/BCS/ADC #&40 (they differ only for A in &80-&BF, i.e. a high byte &82-&C2, never reached). TXA; ADC #7 with C=1 gives the same A and carry as CLC; ADC #8 (no SED anywhere in src/). Exit A = X = the line as before; C dead (CLC at 1526); V not live. No self-modified operands in the lines; mask_operand/pix_operand etc. after it are referenced by label and the writers at 1298-1320 follow them. Caveat for the gate, not a refutation: the 6 bytes come out of DATA1 ahead of everything up to SKIP PAD_END, so sprite_column_count, ck_*, straight_sprite_lo/hi, bank 4's straight sprites and the render variables all move down 6. Recounted: LDA straight_sprite_hi,X (&A501 -> &A4FB) then crosses a page for every sprite >= 5: +1 on each of ~4.55 executions a pass (up to +4.55); straight_sprite_lo stops crossing at X=&4B, ck_index (&A3CF -> &A3C9) stops crossing for Y &31-&36, list_y1 (&A2EC -> &A2E6) crosses for X >= &1A instead of >= &14 (all savings); and (d_ptr),Y/(col_ptr),Y crossings in bank 4's straight sprites (&A54D on) shift by 6, data-dependent either way. So the 35.7 a pass is the window's figure; the net is likely ~30 but only the gate's measurement settles it. No branch in bank 4 changes its page-crossing status (all 184 checked against the listing shifted by 6).

Checked in src/render.6502. Entry to up_cell is only the fall-through of TXA/BPL raised (1498-1499), where X = A = the line from TAX at 1482 (clip_test -> BCS visible touches A, flags, ds_j only, never X), and the loop's BCC up_cell, where the new TAX after ADC keeps X = A; so dropping the TAX at the top is exact. Exit at .raised: BPL path A = X from TXA; loop exit A = X from the new TAX, so the removed TAX at .raised is redundant; ORA s_ptr gives the same A/N/Z, C is dead until CLC at 1526, Y = 8 untouched. SBC #&02 never borrows because s_ptr+1 is in &40-&7F: b_ptr+1 comes from raise_address (X = movers_screen_address_high, which the game keeps in the ring via add_delta_to_screen_address_in_AX's BPL/SBC #&40 wrap; raise_address subtracts at most &15 and wraps below &40), the flipped adjust (BPL/SBC #&40), next's forward (INC/BPL/LDA #&40) and step_back (CMP #&40/LDA #&7F), and compiled_part's unsafe restore of the saved b_ptr; after the first iteration ORA #&40 keeps it in &40-&7F. With A in &3D-&7F, ORA #&40 equals CMP #&40/BCS/ADC #&40 (C=0) exactly, and TXA; ADC #7 with C = 1 gives A + 8 and the same carry as CLC; ADC #8. Labels up_cell/raised are local to draw_column's scope and referenced only at 1499 and 1516; up_in_ring only at 1509. Not in tools/grind_config.py PROTECT, not generated, not data, not raster-timed (renderer in the main loop), only zero-page renderer scratch s_ptr (&C2/&C3) and registers touched, so paging (ROMSEL bank 4, ANDY, ACCCON X) is irrelevant and the same RAM is written. Bank 4 renderer shrinks by 6 bytes (fits trivially; references are symbolic). Recount: .raised executes 13.1 a pass (TAX 26.2 cycles in the window), 2 cycles each; loop ~1.9 iterations a pass (TAX 3.8), saving TAX 2 + CMP 2 + BCS taken 3 + CLC 2 - ORA 2 - TAX 2 = 5 each (ADC #&40 path measured 0.0); 26.2 + 9.5 = 35.7 a pass. Bytes: TAX, CMP #, BCS, ADC #, CLC, TAX (9) removed, ORA #, TAX (3) added = 6.

summary: Conservative alternative to the first candidate (overlaps it): only move the cell-up loop's TAX from its top to its bottom, so the hot path into .raised (A = X from the TXA) needs no TAX.
equivalence: Hot path (TXA; BPL raised): A = X already, so the TAX at .raised is redundant. Loop: the TAX moves from the top of up_cell to after ADC #8, so X is updated each iteration (entry X = the line from the TAX at 1482, or via clip_test -> BCS visible, which leaves X alone) and A = X on the fall-through. TAX leaves C, so BCC tests the ADC's carry as before. Everything else unchanged; after .raised A = X = the line, Y = 8, C not live (CLC at 1526 next). No other references to up_cell/raised in src/.
relies_on: Nothing beyond the code shown: X holds the line on every entry to .visible (TAX at 1482; clip_test does not change X).

skeptics.reason: Not refuted. Entries: .visible reached by fall-through from on_same_page (X = line from TAX at 1482; LDA/SEC/ADC/STA/BCC/INC/BIT leave X) or BCS visible from clip_test (LDA/BIT/SBC/DEC A/CMP/STA only, X untouched); up_cell/up_in_ring/raised are referenced only inside this scope (grep of src/: BPL raised, BCC up_cell, BCS up_in_ring), no tables or label+N uses. Path BPL raised: A = X from TXA; old TAX was a no-op on A/X/C/V and its N,Z are overwritten by ORA s_ptr, so dropping it is exact. Loop: the body (LDA s_ptr .. STA s_ptr+1) never reads X, so moving TAX from the loop top to after ADC #8 gives the same X at every loop top; TAX keeps C and V so BCC tests the ADC carry as before; on fall-through A = X = line, C = 1, V from ADC, same as old after its TAX; N,Z overwritten by ORA. Afterwards Y = 8 then LDY #9, X used at 1534 (TXA) = line in both. BCC up_cell still short. No memory or stack difference; the interrupt sees nothing different. Saves 2 cycles (TAX) on every pass through .raised and 1 byte; loop iterations cost the same.

Machine lens: all opcodes are NMOS/65C02 base; no Rockwell/WDC extras. Path (a) TXA; BPL raised: X = line from TAX at 1482 (clip_test -> BCS visible never touches X), so the old TAX at .raised is a no-op: -2 cycles. Path (b) loop: the TAX moves from the top of up_cell to after ADC #8; TAX sets only N/Z so BCC still tests the ADC carry; on entry X already = A (TXA 1498), on the back edge X = new A, the body never reads X, exit A = X as before: per-iteration cost unchanged, exit -2. X after .raised is read only at 1534 (TXA) and is the line in both; C not live (CLC 1526). Bytes -1. BPL raised (&9C1D -> &9C38) and BCC up_cell (&9C37 -> &9C1F, same offset) stay in page &9C. A scan of every branch in the render section of build/strykers.lst (lines 7050-9707, to &B2B5), with the code from &9C39 moved down one byte, finds no branch whose page-crossing changes. The later self-modified operands (mask_operand, pix_operand, *_2) are written by label, so moving them keeps them right; their tables are in game.6502 and hist0/hist1 sit at fixed REN_BASE offsets. Nothing else in src/ refers to up_cell, raised or up_in_ring; no code read as data; the render_end ASSERT only loosens. The claim of 2 cycles per execution (13.1 a pass) and 1 byte stands.

Checked src/render.6502 1453-1530. Entries to .visible: fall-through from on_same_page (X = line from TAX at 1482; LDA/ADC/STA/BCC/INC col_ptr+1/BIT leave X) and BCS visible from clip_test (only A, flags, ds_j touched; X untouched). After TXA, A = X. BPL raised: old TAX at .raised was X=A=X, a no-op; N/Z it set are overwritten by ORA s_ptr. Loop: up_cell only entered by fall-through with A = X, so the removed top TAX was a no-op on iteration 1; on later iterations the new TAX after ADC #8 sets X as the old top TAX did; on fall-through A = X as the old .raised TAX made it. TAX keeps C (and V), so BCC still tests ADC's carry. up_cell/raised are local to the draw_column scope, no other references, no self-modified operand in the lines, no PROTECT entry, not a generated source, no data/zero page meaning changed. Memory accessed is identical (s_ptr, v_ptr only), so ROMSEL &84/&04 and ACCCON X state are irrelevant. Saves 2 cycles on every drawn column (one TAX fewer, on either path) and 1 byte; render.6502 has 102 bytes free, it shrinks. The following bank 4 tables move down 1 byte, but no ALIGN/page ASSERT after line 1500 (ASSERTs at 724-729 are above), they are referenced by label; any page-crossing cycle change is for the gate's measurement, not a correctness issue.

Cycles, pass-through path: old LDY 4 + LDA 4 + BMI 2 + JSR 6 + (LDA 4 STA 3 LDA 4 STA 3 RTS 6) + LDA 4 = 40; new LDA 4 + BMI 2 + STA zp 3 + LDA 4 + STA zp 3 + LDA 4 = 20. BMI-taken: 11 -> 7. old:
STX ren_i
    TXA
    CLC
    ADC boff
new:
STX ren_i
    TXA                             \ C = 0: CPY act_n found Y < act_n
    ADC boff
summary: close_over_overlaps .gather: drop the CLC, since C=0 from CPY act_n not-equal (Y counts up from 0 by one and stops at act_n, so Y < act_n here); STY/LDX/STX/TXA leave C alone.
equivalence: The only way into this code is the gather loop head: CPY act_n; BEQ gathered falls through only when Y != act_n. Y is 0 on the first pass (LDY #0) and ren_k+1 thereafter (from .not_listed, which every path reaches), ren_k being the previous Y; act_n is not written in close_over_overlaps or anything it calls (list_live, list_recorded, list_finish, widen_by_live, world_of_address - grep: act_n written only at render.6502 393/440, before mark_to_draw), and ren_k only by the STY here. So Y increases by 1 from 0 and stops at act_n (<= MOVER_SLOTS), hence Y < act_n when not equal and CPY leaves C=0. STY abs, LDX abs,Y, STX abs, TXA do not affect C, so ADC boff sees C=0 exactly as after CLC. Every later state identical.
relies_on: act_n constant during close_over_overlaps and Y never exceeding it; ren_k not written by the subroutines called from the loop.

skeptics.reason: The only entry to .gather's body is the fall-through of CPY act_n / BEQ gathered (.gather is local to close_over_overlaps' scope, reached only from LDY #0 and BRA gather after .not_listed; every path through the body, shown/listed/not_listed, reaches LDY ren_k / INY). Y starts at 0 and steps by 1; act_n is written only by STZ/INC in step 1 (render.6502 393, 440) before mark_to_draw/close_over_overlaps, and no callee (list_live, list_recorded, list_finish, widen_by_live, world_of_address) writes act_n or ren_k (their stores go to list_*, wa_* only; list_slot etc. lie after act_n/ren_k and are indexed <= MOVER_SLOTS within their MOVER_SLOTS+1 size). So at the body Y < act_n unsigned and CPY leaves C=0; STY abs, LDX abs,Y, STX abs, TXA leave C alone, so ADC boff sees C=0 as after CLC. No exit or flag state differs (CLC changed only C, which was already 0). An interrupt saves and restores P, so it cannot change C between CPY and ADC. Stack untouched. Saves CLC: 2 cycles, 1 byte per execution.

Checked the source. close_over_overlaps is entered only by JSR at render.6502:449 and gather only from LDY #0 or from not_listed (LDY ren_k; INY; BRA gather). act_n is written only at 393 and 440 (classify, before mark_to_draw) and is at most MOVER_SLOTS, so Y counts up from 0 with no wrap. Whenever BEQ gathered falls through, Y < act_n, and CPY act_n leaves C=0. ren_k (EQUB at 2259) and act_n (2265) are written by name only in render.6502, and not inside list_live, list_recorded, list_finish, widen_by_live or world_of_address. Their indexed writes (list_* arrays, X <= MOVER_SLOTS, each MOVER_SLOTS+1 long) cannot reach these bytes. STY abs, LDX abs,Y, STX abs and TXA leave C alone, so ADC boff sees C=0 as it did after CLC. Every opcode is plain NMOS/65SC12. Removing CLC saves 2 cycles and 1 byte on every execution, with no page-crossing or branch-taken path involved. The only branch across the removed byte, BRA gather (backward), gets shorter and stays in range. No self-modifying operand or code read as data in this window. Bank 4 code after this point moves down a byte; the build's ASSERTs and the timing gate catch any branch that crosses a page differently afterwards.

Checked the source. .gather is reached only from LDY #0 at entry and from .not_listed (LDY ren_k; INY; BRA gather); every path (list_live, list_recorded, widen_by_live, listed) falls to .not_listed. act_n is written only at render.6502 393 (STZ) and 440 (INC), both in classify before close_over_overlaps; ren_k only by STY at 458/474/515/852/898. Called routines (list_recorded, list_live, list_finish, widen_by_live, world_of_address) store only to list_*, wa_* and list arrays indexed by list_n <= MOVER_SLOTS, which are sized MOVER_SLOTS+1 and sit after act_n/act, so neither ren_k nor act_n can be hit. Hence Y climbs by 1 from 0 and BEQ exits at Y = act_n, so on fall-through Y < act_n unsigned and CPY leaves C=0; STY/LDX abs,Y/STX/TXA leave C alone (an IRQ restores P on RTI), so ADC boff sees C=0 as after CLC. Not a PROTECTED line, not generated or data, not raster-timed; runs in bank 4 with the same RAM touched; it only shrinks the code by a byte (the hist ASSERTs and render_end ASSERT would catch any layout break at build time). Same state on every path, front end included (the renderer runs only in play).

old:
LDA rec_xh,Y
    CMP #&FF
    BNE shown
    LDA need,X
new:
LDA rec_xh,Y
    INC A                           \ 65C02 opcode: Z set if &FF (not shown)
    BNE shown
    LDA need,X
summary: close_over_overlaps .gather: CMP #&FF -> INC A for the not-shown test (same cycles, one byte smaller); A and C after it are dead on both paths.
equivalence: Z after INC A is set iff A was &FF, as after CMP #&FF, so the branch is the same. Differences: A (rec_xh+1 rather than rec_xh), C (carry from ADC boff rather than CMP's), N. Shown path: list_recorded starts LDX list_n; LDA ren_i (A overwritten), reads no flag before LDA/AND, then JMP list_finish which starts STA list_y (A from rec_wy,Y); SEC - C never read before being set. Fall-through: LDA need,X overwrites A and N,Z; AND #&40/BEQ use Z from that; not_listed goes LDY ren_k/INY/BRA gather/CPY (C overwritten); list_live begins LDX/LDY/TYA/STA/LDA/AND/STA/LDA/LDX/JSR world_of_address, which begins SEC. So nothing reads A, N or C from here. 2 cycles either way; 1 byte saved.
relies_on: list_recorded, list_finish, list_live and world_of_address not reading C or A on entry (render.6502 967-1010, 2149-2151). Independent of the CLC candidate (they do not overlap) and of candidate 1.

skeptics.reason: Checked render.6502 891-926, 967-1010, 1042-1050, 2149-2151. INC A sets Z iff A was &FF, as CMP #&FF does; V and D untouched by both; memory and stack untouched (register op, so the interrupt sees nothing different). Only entry to the changed lines is fall-through from TAY in close_over_overlaps (labels shown/not_listed/listed are local to its scope; the classify loop's own 'shown' at 404/418 is a different scope; close_over_overlaps is only JSRed from 449). Shown exit: list_recorded LDX/LDA overwrite A,N,Z; C not read before SEC in list_finish; after return LDX/LDA/AND set N,Z, and widen_by_live begins LDA/PHA/LDA/STA/JSR list_live, whose C on entry comes from list_finish, not from here. Fall-through exit: LDA need,X overwrites A,N,Z; not_listed goes LDY/INY/BRA gather then CPY act_n sets C (and gathered -> STZ/LDX/CPX sets C); list_live starts LDX/LDY/TYA/... /JSR world_of_address which begins SEC before SBC. No path reads A, N or C produced by the changed instruction. INC A is used elsewhere in the source with Baron, so it assembles. CMP #imm 2 bytes/2 cycles, INC A 1 byte/2 cycles: 0 cycles, 1 byte saved.

INC A (&1A) is a real 65C02/65SC12 opcode, 1 byte, 2 cycles, already used throughout render.6502 (lines 414, 639) so Baron accepts it in this cmos section; CMP #&FF is 2 bytes, 2 cycles. Z after INC A is set iff A was &FF, same as CMP #&FF; V untouched by both. BNE shown has the same taken/not-taken timing and its range shrinks by one byte. Checked consumers: shown -> list_recorded overwrites A (LDA ren_i), sets N/Z by loads, then list_finish STA list_y/SEC before any C use; after return LDX/LDA/AND/BEQ reset flags before widen_by_live. Fall-through: LDA need,X/AND/BEQ overwrite A,N,Z; not_listed LDY/INY/BRA gather/CPY act_n sets C; list_live overwrites A (TYA) and world_of_address begins SEC. No self-modifying operand here (rec_xh is fixed workspace at REN_BASE+&180, nothing stores into this code), no code-as-data. Shrinking bank 4 code by one byte moves later code/tables but render_end <= REN_BASE ASSERT only gains slack; any page-crossing change downstream is for the gate's measurement, not this window. 0 cycles, 1 byte.

The case x high > right high branches straight to its RTS because C is already 1.

Y>right_high: the old code (BEQ not taken, SEC, RTS) exits with C=1, N/Z from the CPY and A X Y unchanged. The new taken BNE to the RTS exits with C=1 already set by the CPY (the BCC was not taken), N/Z from the CPY and A X Y V unchanged, so the state is identical. The byte count is unchanged (2 bytes added before, 2 removed): check_if_mover_Y_is_on_screen moves from &2109 to &210B and check_if_mover_is_on_screen from &210D to &210F; is_left_of_viewport_right stays at &211D and nothing after it moves. Every branch (the BNE back to &210A, the BCCs back to &2109 from about &211B, &212A and &212E) stays in page &21, so there is no page-crossing penalty and all are in range. grep finds no absolute or offset references to these labels anywhere.

skeptics.reason: Checked every entry and exit. The line before the moved SEC is change_pixel_tables' RTS (2621), so nothing falls into it. The only references are by name: JSRs at game 2304, 4196 and 5056 and render 872, and BCCs at 2637, 2646 and 2649. Checked against the source. The VIA accesses inside SEI..PLP are the same: PORTB=&03, DDRA=&7F, ORA=key, read ORA, PORTB=&0B, in the same order. The gaps between them are the same too (LDA# and LDX# are both 2 cycles; STA abs and STX abs are both 4 with the same 1 MHz stretch). Note: the code grows 9 bytes (bytes -9 under the skill's positive = smaller convention is correct), which shifts the render workspace labels after it (list_y at $A23C etc.) by 9. Machine lens: not refuted, but the per-pass figure is too high. Opcodes: STZ abs,X (9E, 5 cycles) and INC A (1A, 2 cycles) are real 65SC12 opcodes and both are already used in this source; there are no Rockwell/WDC-only opcodes. Recount from list_finish = &98A4: every branch and its target stay in page &98 (the new block ends at about &98D1), so no taken branch pays a page crossing. Assembled in a scratch copy with Baron (--opt 2): it assembles, and every ASSERT holds. B2 C4 is LDA (zp), a real 65C02/65SC12 opcode at 5 cycles, and the section is cmos. Everything else matches. The JSR at take_off is the only entry, and take_off reloads Y. No self-modified operand is involved: the * + 1 labels come before the edit and do not move. Tables that already straddle a page (for example ck_index, &A3CF->&A3DA) cross at different indices, and sprite (zp),Y reads can gain or lose crossings. pcprof in the gate should confirm the net 46 cycles a pass.

Checked against src/render.6502. restore_block (1795) is reached only by the JSR at 1124 (take_off), and that caller reloads Y from rb_index afterwards. No line is PROTECTED and the code is not generated, data or raster-timed. Neither overlaps rb_end or rb_part2, so swapping the order of the two blocks gives the same values. ROMSEL and ACCCON do not change inside the sequence, so every read hits the same RAM as before, and the interrupt touches none of these bytes. On exit Y is 1 instead of rb_index, and A and the flags differ, but nothing reads them: each_part sets A and the flags; its part path does LDY rb_index and its own CLC; no_part does DEX/DEX/BPL; the exit does LDY rb_index; columns does LDY #10. The 65SC12 has LDA (zp), opcode B2, and the file already uses STA (zp). Cycles: old LDY #3 (2) + 4 x (LDA (zp),Y 5 + STA abs,Y 5 + DEY 2) + BPL 3+3+3+2 = 61, plus LDY rb_index (absolute, 4) = 65. New: 2 + 3 x (5 + 4) + 2 x DEY (2) + LDA (zp) 5 + STA abs 4 = 42. The saving is 23. Page crossings are the same in both: the Y=1..3 reads are identical, and the Y=0 read never crosses. Size: +11 bytes (24 new against 13 old), against 102 free in bank 4 (SKILL.md Room) and ASSERTed. Moving later code by 11 bytes can change which branches cross a page; the gate's cycle measurement catches that, and it is not a correctness fault.

The new code moves that store and load to v_ptr (&C4, zero page). v_ptr is dead from the header copy until STA v_ptr at 1833: nothing in 1826-1832 reads it, and columns, called afterwards, reads the value that 1833 sets. So its in-between value is never seen, and rb_p8 still ends up as start + offset - 8. LDA zp sets N/Z as LDA abs did, and STA/LDA leave C alone, so SEC/SBC #8 are unaffected. Only the part path runs these lines (measured 2.55 times a pass: 10.2 cycles / 4).

A after PLA equals the ADC low result as LDA rb_p8 gave; PLA sets N/Z from it like LDA; C and V come from the ADC at 1827 in both versions (STA/LDA/PHA/PLA leave them alone) and SEC overwrites C anyway. The low byte of rb_p8 written at 1825 is read only at 1829 and is overwritten at 1832 (STA rb_p8) before any other read (1841); no other source or listing reference to &A355/&A356, and the IRQ handler does not touch renderer workspace. No TSX/stack-peek in render or the IRQ (the only TXS is at start-up in game.6502).

rb_p8 is an absolute EQUB in bank 4 (&A3F3 in the listing), not zero page: old STA abs (4c, 3B) + LDA abs (4c, 3B) = 8c/6B; new PHA (3c, 1B) + PLA (4c, 1B) = 7c/2B on the 65SC12, both real NMOS opcodes, no page-crossing or branch effects in the window. PLA sets N/Z from the value like LDA; C (from ADC, consumed nowhere before SEC) and V are untouched by both. The low byte stored at 1825 is read only at 1829 (grep: rb_p8 used only in restore_block, not in any IRQ or self-modified operand; no labels or '= * + n' inside the window); 1832 rewrites it before 1841 reads it. Stack is balanced before PHX/JSR columns; SP set to &FF at entry, one extra byte of depth only. Saves 1 cycle and 4 bytes per execution.

Nothing in src/ stores into this code: there are no label+1/+2 writes and no '= * + 1' labels here, and the bytes are not read as data. wa_off is an EQUB at line 2282 in bank 4 (&9000+), so LDA wa_off+1 is LDA abs: 3 bytes, 4 cycles, no indexing and no page crossing. TXA is 1 byte, 2 cycles, a real 65SC12 opcode (&8A). It sets N and Z from the same value and leaves C from the CMP for the SBC at 2163, which overwrites N, Z, V and C anyway. The SBC abs,Y page-crossing cost is the same in both versions. BCC row_known still jumps over the 1-byte INY, so the range is fine. Saves 2 cycles and 2 bytes on every path.

Checked src/render.6502 2149-2198: world_of_address has one entry (callers at 995 and 2135, both JSR to the label), no label between the TAX at 2158 and the LDA at 2162, and LDY abs,X / LDA abs / CMP abs,Y leave X alone, so X = wa_off+1 (0..63) at 2162. TXA sets N,Z only, keeping C from the CMP for the SBC, and the SBC rewrites N,Z,V. wa_off+1 is still stored and read at 2171; X on exit is unchanged (still wa_off+1), so callers see the same registers. Not PROTECTED, not generated, not raster-timed; reads no different RAM under any ROMSEL/ACCCON state (wa_off is bank-4 workspace, TXA touches no memory). Shrinking render.6502 by 2 bytes fits its region; the hist/rec workspace is at fixed REN_BASE offsets so its ASSERTs are unaffected; later render labels shift by 2 as any code shrink does (page-cross cost of indexed tables is for the gate's measurement). LDA abs 4 cycles/3 bytes vs TXA 2 cycles/1 byte.

Machine lens, checked against the source and the bench listing (build/strykers-shift256end-debug_lives.lst). Opcodes: STX zp, LDX abs,Y, STX zp, CLC/SEC, ADC/SBC zp, TAY, TXA and LDA zp are all NMOS opcodes, so they are valid on the 65SC12; none of BBR/BBS/RMB/SMB is used. Flags: LDX, TAY, LDA and STX leave C alone, so the low byte's carry or borrow reaches the high ADC/SBC. In binary mode ADC is commutative, so A, C, V, N and Z are the same for dh+hi+C as for hi+dh+C (D is clear in play, and old and new both use ADC anyway). SBC keeps its operand order (A=hi, M=dh). The STX delta_high between the high ADC and the BPL changes no flag. Both exits leave A=Y=low byte, X=high byte and delta_low/delta_high=dl[Y]/dh[Y], the same as before. Cycles: the old helper is JSR 6 + PHA 3 + LDA abs,Y 4 + STA 3 + LDA abs,Y 4 + STA 3 + PLA 4 + RTS 6 = 33. The tables are at &1D94-&1DA5 (ship) and &1D98-&1DA9 (bench) and Y is 0..8, so neither table read crosses a page. Add: old 33+12=45, new 3+4+3+2+3+4+2+2+3+3=29, saving 16. Subtract: old 45, new 3+4+3+2+3+4+2+3+3+3=30, saving 15. Weighted: (16x3.03+15x2.35)/5.38=15.56. Bytes: add 10->19, subtract 10->20, helper's 13 removed: 33->39, so the code is 6 bytes larger and bytes saved is -6, as claimed. Branches: BPL skips 3 bytes and BCS skips 2, both in range. Self-modifying code: nothing writes into these routines or the deltas tables (grep for label+1/+2, skip_wraparound_*, leave_1d68). There are no raw numeric absolute addresses in &1D00-&33FF anywhere in src/. The page-sensitive ASSERTs (the green pixel and mask tables at &0440, sound_data_0880) are either at fixed addresses or before the change. The code after the change moves up 6 bytes. In irq1_handler's protected span, BEQ not_vsync_2ee3 (&2DAD bench, &2DA9 ship, both +6) and BNE to_leave_irq1_handler stay within page &2D. wait_for_vsync_2242's BEQ (&22D2 -> &22D8, target &22D6) stays within page &22. So the protected raster timing is unchanged. Interrupts: irq1_handler and sfx_tick do not touch &B6/&B7. The title IRQ handler runs only on the front end, where these routines are not called. On its own the change fits the 31 bytes free before &3400, and the build's ASSERT guards it.

Not refuted. I checked the semantics by hand. On the add path A = dh+hi+C, which gives the same A, C, V, N and Z as before because addition commutes. On the subtract path A = hi-dh-borrow, as before. delta_low and delta_high still end as dl[Y] and dh[Y], so rows_up's &79/&02 leftovers hold, and so does what the logic reads at &B6/&B7 after a render (&B7 is also frame_and_flip). The temporary &B7 = hi could only be seen by an interrupt. irq1_handler, sfx_tick and the title IRQ chain (update_scrolltext, plot_title_screen_character, multiply) never name &B6/&B7 or any of their aliases, and the MOS IRQ does not use &B0-&BF. Every caller is a JSR in game.6502; none is in render.6502 or the banks. The tables are below &3000 and Y 0..8 does not cross a page, so the RAM read is the same whatever ROMSEL or ACCCON's X bit hold. get_screen_address_delta has no other callers. The lines are not protected and not generated. Room: the code grows by 6 bytes (39 against 33), and 31 are free before &3400. Everything after &1DB2 moves +6, by label only: nothing in src/ names an address in that range as a number. The protected irq1_handler span becomes &2DA3-&2DF6, all in page &2D, with no indexed reads. wait_for_vsync_2242's loop stays within one page. The interrupt's variables stay below &3000 (ASSERTed). Shadow &3000-&3FFF is copied from main at render_reset, so the moved code and data there stay mirrored. Nothing from &3400 up changes. One side effect: irq1's BPL no_flip no longer crosses a page, so the code after the palette writes takes 1 cycle less. Cycles: add 45 -> 29 (16 saved), subtract 45 -> 30 (15 saved). Weighted: 83.7 a pass, 15.55 an execution. Bytes saved: -6.

On widen_by_live, the first instruction is LDA list_n, list_live starts with LDX list_n, and A/X/N/Z are rewritten before use. C is untouched. V: grep finds no BVC, BVS, CLV, PHP or PLP anywhere in src/ or src/lib/, so V has no reader all the way back to the game. Stack depth is unchanged. An interrupt saves and restores P and the registers, and it sees no difference in memory. Test assembly in a scratch copy with Baron --opt 2: BIT need,X assembles to 3C EB A1 at &97F8, BVC at &97FB (50 03), JSR widen_by_live at &97FD and .listed at &9800. That is a taken branch from next-PC &97FD to &9800, crossing a page as the old BEQ (next &97FF to &9802) did, so both outcomes save exactly the AND #imm: 2 cycles. need moves from &A1ED to &A1EB. The page-cross penalty is the same for old and new at either address; the effects elsewhere are left to the gate.

BIT abs,X (&3C) is a real 65C02/65SC12 opcode, legal in this cmos section (the routine already uses BRA/STZ); need is &A1ED, absolute, so it assembles as abs,X. 65C02 BIT abs,X is 4 cycles +1 on a page cross, the same rule as LDA abs,X, and need+X (X = ren_i < MOVER_SLOTS = &22) crosses for X >= &13 in both, so the read costs the same. BVC branches iff bit 6 of need[ren_i] is 0, exactly when AND #&40 set Z. Current listing: BEQ at &97FD, fall-through &97FF, .listed &9802: taken = 4 (page cross). New: BIT &97F8, BVC &97FB, fall-through &97FD, .listed &9800: taken = 4 (still crosses), not taken 2 in both; BVC range trivially fine. So old 4+p+2+{2|4} vs new 4+p+{2|4}: 2 cycles saved on both outcomes, 2 bytes. A after: not read on either continuation (.listed -> INC/LDY/INY/BRA gather -> CPY act_n then TXA or the gathered path's LDA need,Y / LDA list_changed; widen_by_live path same). N/Z rewritten before any read. V: there is no BVC/BVS anywhere in src/ (grepped all .6502), so V has no reader even through PHP/PLP. C untouched. No self-modified operands or labels inside the changed lines. The -2 byte shift of the rest of the renderer and its workspace (need, act, list_*) is assembly-time relocated; the hist0/column_buffer page ASSERTs would fail the build loudly if broken, and changed page-crossing elsewhere is left to the gate's measurement as the claim says.

Flipped, C=0: the old code stores b_ptr+1 + 0, the same value.     ROR keys_pressed_bitmap         \ key Y-1 in at bit 7: after eight, key N is bit N

Each key's bit goes in by ASL A/ROR into a bitmap seeded with an &80 sentinel, and the sentinel falling out into carry ends the loop. No shift loop, no zeroing, no CPY.     LDA pixel_table_address_low
    BEQ steps_limited               \ zero if flipped

    LDA walk_d                      \ ...but no more than d + 1
    CLC

    LDA pixel_table_address_low     \ ...and d + 1 steps (d < 255 here),
    BNE walk_beyond_steps
    INX                             \ but none if flipped with n = 0
    BEQ walked

The interrupt runs with I set and no NMI touches these bytes, so the main code's writes (game.6502 3714-3717; render.6502 227, 533, 588; prebuild.6502 58-60 only reads) are atomic with respect to these reads. The only entry is the fall-through from INC field_count (no label inside the window). The exits are no_flip (two branches, as before) and the fall-through to LDA #&0C. At LDA #&0C, A and all the flags are dead. At no_flip, BIT irq_owned sets N, V and Z, and then A is overwritten by LDA #&02 or by PLA. The one difference is C: before, C was 1 (from CMP #&82) whenever flip_pending was clear; now it is the result of CMP flip_target. Removed PHA (3 cycles, 1 byte) and PLA (4 cycles, 1 byte); LDA &F4 (3) only moves after the JSR, so 7 cycles and 2 bytes per execution. Equivalence: ROMSEL gets &05 then the value of &F4 in both; I checked src/lib/sfx50.6502 in full (sfx_tick, sfx_next_ramp incl. the self-modified ramp operand at ramp+1/+2 in bank 5, sfx_output, sfx_write): no write to &F4 (romsel_copy/os_ram_copy_of_currently_selected_rom), &FE30 or ACCCON, no CLI/PLP on sfx_tick's path (sfx_silence's PHP/SEI/PLP is not called from it), no MOS calls, no stack reads; its variables are in bank 5 (&A5A7 on). PLA loads v, STA &FC (zero-page RAM, not I/O) keeps v, PLY/PLX touch only X, Y, N, Z, so A is already v at RTI; the dropped LDA &FC only re-sets N/Z, which RTI overwrites from the stacked P. No CLI between entry and RTI (none in irq1_handler or src/lib/sfx50.6502; the game's CLIs are at start-up/elsewhere), and an NMI touching &FC in the 3-cycle gap would make the new code the more correct one. &FC is still stored, so anything reading it later (bank5 title_screen_irq1_handler chain, MOS) sees the same value; on the front end, when title_screen_irq1_handler chains in, the value pushed and popped is the same and the T1 path still ends with A=v. equivalence: After STA acccon, A = (ACCCON AND &FE) OR flip_screen (the register value, not a re-read of ACCCON). AND #&01 gives bit 0 of that = flip_screen's bit 0 = flip_screen, since flip_screen is written only by render.6502:531 from `back` = shown_screen EOR 1, and shown_screen is only STZ'd or set from flip_screen, both starting at 0, so it is 0 or 1 by induction. STA shown_screen stores the same byte; Z/N differ only transiently (A=0/1 either way gives the same Z, N=0 both) and the next instruction STZ then BIT irq_owned sets N,Z,V anyway. No label between the lines; entry only by fall-through from STA acccon.
relies_on: flip_screen in {0,1} (render.6502 back = shown_screen EOR 1); A unchanged since ORA flip_screen (STA does not change A). Shrinks the handler by 1 byte (interrupt variables move down by 1, symbol-referenced; combined with the other two candidates 5 bytes).

skeptics.reason: Entry only by fall-through from STA acccon (no label between game.6502:4523 and .no_flip; nothing branches in). At that point A = (ACCCON AND &FE) OR flip_screen, untouched by STA, so AND #&01 = bit 0 of flip_screen. flip_screen's only writer is render.6502:531 (STA flip_screen from back); back's only writer is render.6502:323 (shown_screen EOR 1); shown_screen is written only by STZ (render.6502:228, 587) and this STA from flip_screen; all start 0 (EQUB 0). By induction flip_screen and shown_screen are always 0 or 1, so the stored byte is identical. Flags: both leave N=0, Z=(flip_screen==0), C/V/D untouched; STZ flip_pending changes none, then .no_flip's BIT irq_owned overwrites N,V,Z and the paths after it (PLA at leave_irq1_handler, or LDA #&02) kill A and test no flag before setting it, and C is not read before RTI restores P. The handler runs with I set, so no nested interrupt between the lines; the main-line readers (render, render_to_main) see the same shown_screen value. No stack change. Cycles: LDA abs 4 -> AND # 2, saves 2; bytes 3 -> 2, saves 1.

Holds on the 65SC12. Old: LDA flip_screen is absolute (&2E5D, not zero page): 4 cycles, 3 bytes, no indexing so no page-crossing term. New: AND #&01 immediate, 2 cycles, 2 bytes, a real 6502 opcode (&29). Saves 2 cycles and 1 byte on the flip path (once per flip), the other paths do not reach it. A at that point is (ACCCON AND &FE) OR flip_screen (STA acccon leaves A alone), so bit 0 is flip_screen's bit 0 and bits 1-7 come from ACCCON. AND #&01 equals flip_screen only if flip_screen is 0 or 1. Checked: flip_screen (EQUB 0) is written in src/ only at render.6502:531 from back (&A18A, bank 4 EQUB 0). back is written only at render.6502:323 as shown_screen EOR 1. shown_screen is written only by STZ (render.6502:228 and 587) and by this handler from flip_screen, so both stay 0 or 1 by induction. No indexed store reaches them: sfx_request,X uses X 0-3 only, and flip_pending, flip_target and irq_owned are never indexed. Flags: N=0 and Z the same either way, C and V are not touched, STA and STZ change no flags, and the BIT irq_owned at .no_flip sets N, V and Z again before any branch. There is no label between the two lines and no self-modifying operand here (previous_irq1_vector_low is later and found by its symbol). The 1-byte shift of the interrupt variables and the code after them up to the SKIP unused_3400_original is reached only through symbols (the tools use syms, ASSERT shown_screen < &3000 still holds, and the sprite tables use LO/HI of labels), and SKIP keeps everything from &3400 where it was. STA ra_lo as before; X = hi as before (and dead until TAX at 1779). After the window the code reads only Y, ra_lo and ra_hi (TYA kills A; SEC sets C before the table SBC). ra_rows is then never read anywhere: only raise_address used it, and the old final value 7-(d AND 7) was dead. Old flags came from LDX; caller does TAY then AND, so N/Z/C/V dead; D never set. Stack: no pushes, RTS on both paths at same depth. Interrupt: nothing in irq1_handler or what it calls reaches raise_address or reads its code bytes; the routine is not re-entrant and the self-modified operands (&9D87, &9D8B in the new layout) are in bank 4 sideways RAM at &9xxx, paged whenever this code runs. New layout: BCC at &9D88 to .up at &9D90, no page cross. Recount: stay 40->26, up 53->43, bytes 52->40.

Machine lens: every opcode and addressing mode is plain 6502 (CMP#, LDA#, SBC/ADC/EOR abs, STA/STY/STX abs). Cycles checked against the listing (raise_address at &9D7E). Stay path: old 40 (STX4 STA4 STY4 AND2 CMP4 BCC2 LDA4 SEC2 SBC4 LDX4 RTS6), new 26 (STA4 STY4 AND2 CMP#2 BCC2 LDA#2 SBC4 RTS6). The candidate is still correct and faster, so it is not refuted; the gate's passbench measures the real net. Moving the bank 4 tables is the project lens's question (the no-data-moves rule).

Exits: old continued to search_for_target_loop iff N=0 after DEX and reached search_done iff N=1; new BPL does exactly the same, as BPL and BMI are complements on N for every X, not just 0..11. Neither JMP nor branches touch A, X, Y, flags, memory or stack, so all are identical at both exits (search_done reloads X and flags from target; the loop head CPX resets C/Z/N). X arrives at consider_next_enemy as 0..11, so DEX leaves -1..10: BPL is taken for 0..10 (the old JMP case) and falls through at &FF (the old BMI-taken case) into search_done, which comes next and is referenced only here. N and Z come from DEX on both, and the first instruction after the exit is LDX target, which sets its own flags; no other flag, register or memory changes. Old exit = BMI taken 3 (same page &2C43 to &2C46) = 3, new = BPL not taken 2, saving 1. So it saves 1 cycle on every execution. Bytes: 2+3 down to 2, saving 3. The line is not PROTECTED and is not generated, data, a table or self-modified. It runs in main RAM below &3000 with no paging or ACCCON dependence.     LDY #0
.move
    LDA cp_len_lo
    ORA cp_len_hi
    BEQ moved
    LDA (v_ptr),Y
    STA (s_ptr),Y
    INY
    BNE counted
    INC v_ptr + 1
    INC s_ptr + 1
.counted
    LDA cp_len_lo
    BNE len_low
    DEC cp_len_hi
.len_low
    DEC cp_len_lo
    BRA move                        \ 65C02 opcode
.moved
    LDA cp_next_lo
    STA cp_cursor_lo
    LDA cp_next_hi
    STA cp_cursor_hi
new:
STA cp_cursor_hi                \ the next block's cursor now: nothing reads cp_cursor_hi again
    LDY #0                          \ copy forward (the block only moves down): whole pages, then
    LDX cp_len_hi                   \ the rest, Y and the pointers as the byte loop had them
    BEQ rest
.whole_pages
    LDA (v_ptr),Y
    STA (s_ptr),Y
    INY
    BNE whole_pages
    INC v_ptr + 1
    INC s_ptr + 1
    DEX
    BNE whole_pages
.rest
    LDX cp_len_lo                   \ the rest, Y = 0 up
    BEQ moved
.rest_byte
    LDA (v_ptr),Y
    STA (s_ptr),Y
    INY
    DEX
    BNE rest_byte
.moved
    LDA cp_next_lo
    STA cp_cursor_lo
summary: Simpler alternative to candidate 1 (same lines): the block move as a whole-page loop plus a remainder loop counted in X (18 cycles a byte instead of 42), the cursor high stored straight into cp_cursor_hi; smaller than the original.
equivalence: Entry: only by fall-through from the block setup (labels move/counted/len_low/moved are local to compact's scope and referenced only inside this loop; grep finds no other use; next_block and all_moved are untouched). cp_cursor_hi: last read at the LDA cp_cursor_hi before the ADC cp_len_hi (line 2048), so storing the new hi there instead of cp_next_hi and copying it at .moved gives cp_cursor_hi the same value by the time next_block / all_moved read it; cp_next_hi is read nowhere else (grep: only lines 2052 and 2074), so it is left stale harmlessly; the interrupt never reads renderer workspace. Copy: the original copies len = cp_len_hi*256+cp_len_lo bytes forward, byte k at (v_ptr)+k to (s_ptr)+k, with Y=k mod 256 and both pointer highs bumped each time Y wraps. The new code does exactly the same addresses in the same ascending order (forward order matters: the destination is at or below the source and may overlap): cp_len_hi whole pages with Y 0..255 and the highs bumped after each page (the original bumps on the same wraps, including when len is an exact multiple of 256), then cp_len_lo bytes with Y from 0 (Y is 0 after the page loop or from LDY #0) up to cp_len_lo-1 <= 254, no wrap. Each (zp),Y access has the same base and Y as the original, so the page-crossing penalties are the same too. len 0, 1, 2, odd, even, and whole pages with lo 0 all checked: lo=0 -> LDX sets Z, BEQ moved; otherwise X counts lo bytes down to 0. Live after: at .moved -> JMP next_block, which reloads A and sets X (LDX #0) and Y (TAY in scan) before reading them; flags dead. Final Y, v_ptr, s_ptr equal the original's (Y = len_lo); X differs (dead); cp_len_lo/hi are left as computed instead of counted to 0: read nowhere else (grep: only render.6502 2038-2069), and the caller (draw_mover's .room) reloads X, Y, v_ptr and s_ptr. Paging: identical addressing modes on the same addresses in each ROMSEL/ACCCON state.
relies_on: cp_cursor_hi not read between line 2052 and .moved; cp_next_hi, cp_len_lo, cp_len_hi read nowhere outside this routine; save blocks move only downward, forward copy order kept; X dead in the loop and after.

skeptics.reason: Checked against src/render.6502 2032-2083 and the workspace at 2313-2322. Entry: only fall-through from the block setup; move/counted/len_low are referenced only inside the loop, and moved stays a target of the new BEQs. cp_cursor_hi is last read at 2048 (LDA cp_cursor_hi before ADC cp_len_hi), so storing the new hi there at 2052 gives next_block (scan never reads it) and all_moved (2081) the same value; cp_len_lo/hi and cp_next_lo/hi are plain EQUBs in bank 4 with no alias (no other label at their addresses) and are read only in compact, so cp_len_* left non-zero and cp_next_hi stale are harmless. Copy: len = hi*256+lo copied in the same ascending order, each (zp),Y with the same base and Y as the old loop (whole pages Y 0..255 with both highs bumped after each wrap, exactly when the old loop bumped them, including lo=0; then lo bytes from Y=0, at most 255, no wrap); empty block (hi=lo=0) copies nothing in both. Final Y (= lo), v_ptr, s_ptr equal the old ones; zero-page writes (&C2-&C5) are the same sequence, so an interrupt between instructions sees the same pointer state; the only other differences are bank-4 workspace bytes the IRQ does not read. X: old exits with cp_best_slot, new with 0; next_block does LDX #0 before any read and all_moved is reached only from scan (LDX back first). Flags and A dead (next_block LDA #&FF). Stack untouched. Caller (.room after JSR compact) reloads X, Y, A. Recount, 65SC12: old per byte 4+4+2+5+6+2+3+4+3+6+3 = 42; new 5+6+2+3 = 16 in whole pages, 5+6+2+2+3 = 18 in the rest: 24 saved a byte in the common (hi=0) case; about 7 more saved a block. Bytes old 49, new 43: 6 saved.

All opcodes and modes are real 65SC12 ones (LDX abs, DEX, (zp),Y on v_ptr=&C4/s_ptr=&C2, INC zp; no BBR/BBS/RMB/SMB). cp_* are abs EQUBs in bank 4 workspace (render.6502 2312-2322), only referenced in compact; cp_cursor_hi is not read between the new store and .moved, and next_block/all_moved see the same value; cp_next_hi is then unread. Copy order, addresses and Y per access match the original for len_hi*256+len_lo (lo=0, exact pages, lo<=255 with no wrap in the rest loop), so the (zp),Y read penalties are the same. X, flags dead (next_block LDX #0, all_moved LDX back). Listing places the code at &9FE5-&A00x: in the new layout whole_pages (&9FEF) and its BNEs stay in page &9F, rest_byte (&A002) and its BNE in page &A0, BEQ moved forward within &A0, so no taken branch crosses a page. The original's BRA move at &A008 -> &9FEA crosses a page (+1), so the old per-byte cost is 43 (4+4+2+5+6+2+3+4+3+6+4), new 18 in the rest loop (5+6+2+2+3) and 16 in the page loop: saving 25 a byte (27 in whole pages), at least the claimed 24. Fixed overhead: new LDX/BEQ/LDX/BEQ 13 against the old final LDA/ORA/BEQ 11 plus the removed LDA cp_next_hi/STA cp_cursor_hi 8. Bytes: old 49, new 43, 6 saved. No self-modified operand or code-as-data in the region.

Checked against src/render.6502 1981-2084. compact is entered only by JSR from draw_mover (line 1153) and the loop only by fall-through; move/counted/len_low/moved are local to compact's scope. cp_cursor_hi is last read at 2048 before the store, and next_block/all_moved read it only after .moved, so storing the new hi there directly gives the same value; cp_next_hi, cp_len_lo/hi are bank-4 renderer workspace (render.6502 2319-2322) read nowhere else; the declarations stay, so no data moves and no RAM is added (cp_next_hi just goes unused). The copy does len = hi*256+lo bytes forward, the same (zp),Y addresses in the same ascending order (destination at or below source, overlap safe), the pointer highs bumped on the same Y wraps, and Y, v_ptr and s_ptr end as the original left them; len 0, lo=0 with hi>0, and hi=0 all checked. X and the flags are dead: next_block does LDX #0, all_moved LDX back, and .room reloads X, Y and the pointers. The addressing modes are the same, so it reads and writes the same RAM in every ROMSEL/ACCCON state (the arena &354A-&3FFF, main or shadow). Not protected, not generated, not raster-timed; 6 bytes smaller, so it fits. Recount: the old loop costs 42 cycles a byte (LDA abs 4, ORA abs 4, BEQ 2, LDA (zp),Y 5, STA (zp),Y 6, INY 2, BNE 3, LDA abs 4, BNE 3, DEC abs 6, BRA 3), the new remainder loop 18 (5+6+2+2+3) and the page loop 16, so it saves 24 a byte (26 inside whole pages), plus a few for setup. Bytes 49 -> 43.
